items.abstract_or_text: # Patch release: v5.20.2 This patch notably solves an issue where some inputs could loose their original type inside `prepare_inputs_for_generation` in `generate`, leading to problems with multimodal models. It also fixes some other issues listed on the below commits. It contains the following commits: - Fix inputs dict casting in generate (#49731) by @Cyrilvallez - Fix zero expert gradients in bfloat16 with expert parallelism and ep_size < fsdp_size (#49688) by @qgallouedec - Declare the input modalities of the VLMs that report text only (#49677) by @qgallouedec - Avoid a host-to-device copy in eager_mask (#49684) by @hmellor

items.abstract_or_text: tests : make MoE router selection independent of the backend noise (#30818) * tests : make MoE router selection independent of the backend noise The router scores are in the range [0, 1), so a random draw can leave the last expert (or expert group) still selected and the first one dropped tied within the noise between the backends. They then route a token to different experts and the logits differ by 4e-3 instead of the usual 5e-7. Beam is the only arch here with a real top-k (8 experts, 2 used) and a group top-k (4 groups, 2 used), so it is the only one that hits this: 2 of 20 seeds failed on an M2 Ultra, the other MoE archs select 2 of 2 and cannot tie. Fill the selection bias with a ramp of step 2 to give every expert a score range of its own, which turns the top-k into a function of the expert index alone. The bias affects only the selection, the weights still come from the unbiased probs, so the MoE output keeps its magnitude. Beam now matches the CPU reference within 4e-7 for all of 160 seeds. Assisted-by: pi:llama.cpp/ggml-org/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF (MacBook, M5 Max, 128GB) * tests : tell the CPU and the GPU of an Apple SoC apart in the device table Both devices report the same description ("Apple M2 Ultra" here), so the device column of the test table had two indistinguishable rows and a failing row did not say whether the Metal device or the host CPU produced it. Add the device name, which is also what -b takes, unless the description already is the name.
